speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This includes cultivating public awareness and appreciation, and weaving thoughtful biophilic designs into our urban spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: At the same time, because we are a densely populated city-state, we will also need to ensure public health and safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To do so, the National Parks Board (NParks) takes a science- and community-based approach to wildlife management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks studies the population trends and distribution of various wildlife species across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The findings of these studies guide the development of NParks’ wildlife management strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks also consults local as well as wildlife experts to ensure that its strategies are in line with international practices and standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In managing different wildlife species, such as pest birds, long-tailed macaques, wild boars and crocodiles, NParks considers factors such as the species’ ecology and behaviour, threats to public health and safety, animal welfare, as well as impact on native biodiversity, habitats and the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Based on an assessment of these factors, a range of measures may be adopted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These include public education, enforcement against illegal wildlife feeding, habitat modification to reduce food sources and translocation of the animals away from urban areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks may also need to take steps to safeguard public safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For instance, it may put up signage to advise the public on how to respond to wildlife sightings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks may also install exclusion measures such as fencing, or carry out direct population control where necessary, such as in the case of wild boars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In the case of estuarine crocodiles, like the one found near Marina East Drive, public safety is a major consideration as they are apex predators and stealthy, opportunistic feeders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: They have attacked and killed children and adults in other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, on 23 October 2023, The Straits Times reported three suspected crocodile attacks in Sabah in the preceding month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To protect the public, the Sabah authorities had to cull five large crocodiles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: When there are sightings of crocodiles in Singapore, NParks will first assess if there is an immediate threat to public safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, if the sighting is at a recreational destination, NParks will trap the crocodile and try to relocate or rehome it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In doing so, NParks takes into account the strong homing instinct of estuarine crocodiles to return to the location of capture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: If there are no suitable options for relocation and rehoming, the crocodile will be humanely put down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This approach is aligned with that taken in many other jurisdictions that have crocodiles or alligators, such as the city of Darwin in Australia's Northern Territory, where crocodiles are actively removed from areas of high human activity to reduce the likelihood of crocodile attacks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These crocodiles are either rehomed or put down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The crocodile that the Member has mentioned was a large adult, measuring around three metres long.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: That is almost one and a half storeys high.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It was sighted around two kilometres away from East Coast Park, which is about a 10-minute swim for a crocodile moving at stealth in the waters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks first explored the option of relocating the crocodile to the Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve, but given the reserve’s large existing crocodile population of around 20 individuals, it no longer has the capacity for more crocodiles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In any case, moving the crocodile away from the Marina East beach would have risked it returning to the site, venturing to East Coast Park, or even straying into another area with high human activity along our coastline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: If so, it would pose a substantial threat to public safety, given its large size and predatory nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks also reached out to the Mandai Wildlife Group (MWG).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, as MWG shared with The Straits Times, multiple factors are considered in zoo population management and planning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These include whether the outcome of a move would favour the animal in terms of quality of life and welfare, and possible negative effects on the zoo’s institutional population planning and conservation commitments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In this case, MWG determined that it would not be able to rehome the crocodile in a way that met these criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The euthanasia was done by a veterinarian, in accordance with international standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks has also put in place other measures to mitigate the risks to public safety from Singapore’s wild crocodile population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, at the Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve, NParks has installed fences to prevent crocodiles from getting onto footpaths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks has also installed signs to alert visitors to the presence of crocodiles and to advise them to remain calm and back away if they encounter a crocodile.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In addition, NParks conducts regular population surveys of the reserve’s crocodiles and is exploring the use of technology to track their movements.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have three follow-up supplementary questions, bearing in mind the more long-term protection and solution to this.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Really, the intention is to understand the structured approach.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, experts mentioned that there are very few studies to understand the behaviour of crocodiles, especially locally.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is that something that we are looking more into doing?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, thank you for sharing the steps which NParks took.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, animal welfare groups (AWGs) and things like that.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The third question is, are groups such as Our Wild Neighbours looking to do more to bring more awareness about such animals so beyond, for example, otters and macaques?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are we also looking into doing more for crocodiles as well as tapirs which we had recently seen in September as well?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, it is not just specific to crocodiles or specific animals – we do it on a large scale.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Importantly, we also regularly consult experts from overseas.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We consult them regularly as part of our effort in Singapore, because they have much more experience dealing with crocodiles in their part of the world.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We adopt best practices from jurisdictions like the Northern Territory as well as other parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, we will continue to engage our stakeholder groups in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And to the Member’s last question, on public education.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that we had to move quickly in terms of public safety, but could I ask whether the framework that the Senior Minister of State has just shared in this House can be put through a consultation with all the animal welfare groups and nature groups, the youth leaders that he talked about, so that there can be consensus in how we move forward in future cases where there are human-wildlife conflict again?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, the framework is not something that is new or unfamiliar to many of our stakeholder groups.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is based on community inputs and, importantly, based on science.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We assess what needs to be done based on internationally informed scientific evidence and how to customise it to our context.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And we welcome inputs from stakeholders on how we should deal with wildlife encounters along the way.
